unit.why: R. Aaron of Karlin tells how the Besht appeared to his son after his death and showed him, through a vision of a mountain and an abyss, how to serve the Creator.
unit.boundary_note: The homiletic frame (R. Aaron of Karlin's moral teaching on toil in divine service) begins in the previous division. The narrative itself is complete here.

stories.end_quote: כך עובדין את הבורא (ס׳ בית אהרן בדרוש לפסח)
stories.summary_en: After his death the Besht appears to his son, who asks how one serves the Creator. The Besht stands on a high mountain above a deep abyss, throws himself down until his limbs break into crumbs, and says: this is how one serves the Creator.

tags.why: The Besht's son is the recipient of the appearance.

quotes: שנראה לבנו אחר פטירתו ושאל אותו איך עובדין את הבורא
tags.why: The son converses with his deceased father's soul.

quotes: ועמד על ראש ההר וזרק א״ע לתוך העמק
tags.why: The son sees a supernatural visionary scene; it is unclear whether he was awake or dreaming.

quotes: ואח״כ א״ל כך עובדין את הבורא
